nodes.description: SCAF4 and SCAF8 act redundantly as anti-terminators that suppress early, alternative polyadenylation sites; SCAF4 is additionally required for termination at canonical distal sites. Loss of SCAF4 in HEK293 cells increases transcriptional read-through or alternative last-exon usage, and combined loss with SCAF8 causes early termination and truncated mRNAs and is lethal. These data come from engineered knockout cell lines, not from patient cells.

evidence.snippet: Here, we describe a role for SCAF4 and SCAF8 as anti-terminators, suppressing the use of early, alternative polyadenylation (polyA) sites.

evidence.reference_title: SCAF4 and SCAF8, mRNA Anti-Terminator Proteins.
evidence.snippet: While SCAF4 and SCAF8 work redundantly to suppress early mRNA termination, they also have independent, non-essential functions. SCAF8 is an RNAPII elongation factor, whereas SCAF4 is required for correct termination at canonical, distal transcription termination sites in the presence of SCAF8.

nodes.description: Heterozygous truncating and splice-site variants spread across SCAF4 are predicted, and for some alleles shown in patient blood RNA, to undergo nonsense-mediated decay or yield severely truncated protein, reducing the dose of SCAF4. SCAF4 binds the RNA polymerase II C-terminal domain phosphorylated on Ser2 and Ser5 through its N-terminal CTD-interacting domain (CID); the few missense variants reported cluster in the CID and are predicted to destabilise it, compatible with the same loss of function.

nodes.description: RNA sequencing of peripheral blood from four individuals with SCAF4 variants, compared with eight controls, showed differential expression of 9,038 genes and differential isoform usage in more than 2,900 genes. A later case with a paternally inherited nonsense variant also showed widespread transcriptional dysregulation in blood RNA. Whether these changes reflect the termination defect seen in knockout cells, and how they relate to neural phenotypes, is not established.
